ca-basa-kho-thom.name: Basa Fish Braised with Pineapple
ca-basa-kho-thom.serving_basis: Four portions of braised fish to serve with steamed rice as part of a family meal.
ca-basa-kho-thom.description: Basa fish is gently braised with golden pineapple and a mild caramel fish-sauce glaze. It pairs easily with steamed rice and blanched vegetables.
ca-basa-kho-thom.finished_dish: The fish steaks are firm yet moist and coated in glossy brown braising liquid; the pineapple is tender with a gentle sweet-and-sour taste, finished with scallions.
ca-basa-kho-thom.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and a plate of blanched or stir-fried greens.
tips: Let the fish drain after rinsing and turn it carefully to keep the steaks intact.
Add pineapple near the end so the pieces hold their shape.
Cook until the fish is opaque throughout and flakes easily with a fork; adjust seasoning before serving.
ca-basa-kho-thom.image_alt: Basa fish braised with pineapple in a clay pot, with glossy brown fish steaks, golden pineapple and scallions.
ca-basa-kho-thom.time_note: About 90 minutes, including marinating; simmer gently so the fish absorbs the sauce while the pineapple keeps its shape.

ingredients.name: Basa fish
ingredients.notes: Cut into medium-thick steaks and drain.

ingredients.name: Pineapple
ingredients.notes: Peel, remove the eyes and cut into pieces.

ingredients.name: Minced shallot and garlic
ingredients.notes: Divide between the marinade and sauteing.

ingredients.name: Minced chili
ingredients.notes: Use less for a milder dish.

ingredients.name: Sugar
ingredients.notes: Divide between marinating and making the caramel.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: Use part of it to make the caramel.

preparation_steps: Rub the fish with a little salt, rinse and drain. Cut it into steaks; peel, core and cut the pineapple.
Mince the shallot, garlic and scallion whites. Marinate the fish with fish sauce, sugar, shallot, garlic, scallion whites and chili for 30 minutes.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil with some sugar over low heat until it turns amber. Add the fish and sear each side gently for 2–3 minutes until firm.
Add the remaining marinade and water, cover and simmer gently. Turn the fish once with care and skim off any foam.
When the fish is nearly cooked, add the pineapple and braise for another 8–10 minutes until the fish is fully cooked and the sauce lightly thickens. Finish with scallions and pepper.

dau-que-xao-thit-heo.name: Stir-Fried Green Beans with Pork
dau-que-xao-thit-heo.serving_basis: One platter of green beans and pork for four people to share with rice.
dau-que-xao-thit-heo.description: Crisp-sweet green beans are stir-fried with thin pork slices and garlic. The everyday ingredients and quick method make this a practical family meal.
dau-que-xao-thit-heo.finished_dish: The beans are green and just tender, the pork is soft and thoroughly cooked, and the garlic is fragrant. The stir-fry is lightly seasoned and not watery.
dau-que-xao-thit-heo.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and a light vegetable soup.
tips: Remove the strings along both sides of the beans and cut evenly so they cook at the same rate.
Add only enough water to soften the beans without leaving the pan watery.
Cook the pork thoroughly before serving.
dau-que-xao-thit-heo.image_alt: A plate of Vietnamese green beans stir-fried with pork, glossy green beans and tender cooked pork slices.
dau-que-xao-thit-heo.time_note: About 35 minutes; stir-fry the beans first with a little water, then add the pork and cook through.

ingredients.name: Green beans
ingredients.notes: Remove the strings, rinse and cut diagonally.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add gradually while softening the beans.

preparation_steps: Remove the strings along both sides of the green beans, rinse and cut diagonally into bite-size pieces. Mince the garlic.
Rinse the pork, drain and slice thinly. Wash your hands, knife and board after handling raw meat.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil over medium heat and toss the beans for about a minute to coat them. Add about half a cup of water, partially cover and cook until the beans are just tender.
Add the pork and stir until it firms up. Season with seasoning powder, salt and optional monosodium glutamate; continue cooking until the pork is fully cooked.
Add the garlic and stir briefly until fragrant. Taste, sprinkle with pepper and serve hot.

cai-lan-xao-nam-dui-ga-chay.name: Vegetarian Chinese Broccoli with King Oyster Mushrooms
aliases: Vegetarian Gai Lan with King Oyster Mushrooms
Vegetarian Chinese Broccoli and Mushroom Stir-Fry
cai-lan-xao-nam-dui-ga-chay.serving_basis: One platter of vegetarian greens to share among four people.
cai-lan-xao-nam-dui-ga-chay.description: Crisp green Chinese broccoli is quickly stir-fried with seared king oyster mushroom rounds and fried garlic. The mushrooms are scored to resemble scallops; no seafood is used.
cai-lan-xao-nam-dui-ga-chay.finished_dish: The Chinese broccoli stems are tender-crisp and bright green; the mushroom rounds are lightly browned, springy and fragrant with garlic.
cai-lan-xao-nam-dui-ga-chay.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice, braised tofu or a simple vegetarian soup.
tips: Peel away fibrous skin from older broccoli stems.
Blanch the vegetables and mushrooms briefly, drain well, then stir-fry the greens over high heat to keep their color.
Choose vegetarian-labeled seasoning powder and oyster-style sauce; this recipe contains no seafood or animal products.
cai-lan-xao-nam-dui-ga-chay.image_alt: A vegetarian plate of Chinese broccoli stir-fried with garlic and scored king oyster mushroom rounds, with no seafood.
cai-lan-xao-nam-dui-ga-chay.time_note: About 30 minutes; blanch briefly, then stir-fry the greens quickly over high heat.

ingredients.name: Chinese broccoli
ingredients.notes: Pick the tender stems and leaves, peel fibrous stems and cut into pieces.

ingredients.name: King oyster mushrooms
ingredients.notes: Cut into thick rounds and lightly score both sides in a diamond pattern.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For frying the aromatics and searing the mushrooms.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian oyster-style sauce
ingredients.notes: Check the label to make sure it is suitable for vegetarian cooking.

preparation_steps: Pick the tender Chinese broccoli, discard wilted leaves, peel fibrous stems and cut into pieces. Rinse and drain.
Cut the king oyster mushrooms into thick rounds and lightly score both sides. Mince the garlic and slice the shallots.
cooking_steps: Briefly blanch the Chinese broccoli and mushrooms in boiling water, then drain. Season the mushrooms with a little vegetarian seasoning powder.
Fry some garlic and shallot until fragrant and set aside. Use the remaining oil to sear the mushroom rounds on both sides until lightly golden.
Stir-fry the Chinese broccoli over high heat with vegetarian seasoning powder, vegetarian oyster-style sauce and salt until just tender. Add the mushrooms, pepper and fried aromatics, then serve hot.

ga-nuong-muoi-ot.name: Vietnamese Chili-Salt Roasted Chicken
ga-nuong-muoi-ot.serving_basis: One medium whole chicken, portioned as a main dish for four people.
ga-nuong-muoi-ot.description: A flattened chicken is marinated in a chili-salt sauce with lemongrass, garlic and dried shrimp, then roasted until golden. It suits a weekend dinner or a larger family meal.
ga-nuong-muoi-ot.finished_dish: The skin is golden and fragrant with a mild chili-salt heat; the meat is cooked through, moist and infused with lemongrass and garlic.
ga-nuong-muoi-ot.serving: Cut into pieces and serve hot with rice or fresh greens; chili-lime salt can be served on the side.
tips: Marinate under refrigeration for at least two hours; do not leave raw chicken at room temperature for an extended period.
Cover the chicken loosely for the first roasting stage so the surface does not brown too quickly.
Check that the thickest part of the thigh reaches at least 74°C before serving.
ga-nuong-muoi-ot.image_alt: Golden Vietnamese chili-salt roasted chicken on a platter with red chili and roasted lemongrass.
ga-nuong-muoi-ot.time_note: About 3 hours 15 minutes, including at least 2 hours of refrigerated marinating and 45 minutes of roasting.

ingredients.name: Whole chicken
ingredients.notes: Choose a medium chicken, clean and drain.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.notes: Remove tough leaves and cut into pieces.

ingredients.name: Fresh chili
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the preferred heat level.

ingredients.name: Coarse salt
ingredients.notes: Grind finely before blending the marinade.

ingredients.name: Chili powder
ingredients.notes: Reserve some for the final roasting stage.

ingredients.name: Honey
ingredients.notes: Balances the heat and helps the surface color; avoid brushing on too early.

preparation_steps: Soak the dried shrimp until softened and drain. Blend with lemongrass, garlic, chili and coarse salt; stir in chili sauce, annatto oil, fish sauce and honey.
Clean the chicken and trim excess fat if desired. Cut along the breastbone and press gently to flatten it, then coat both sides with the sauce.
Marinate the chicken in a covered container in the refrigerator for at least two hours. Wash hands and sanitize surfaces after handling raw poultry.
cooking_steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Place the chicken on a tray, cover loosely with foil and roast for 30 minutes.
Remove the foil, brush lightly with reserved sauce or chili powder and roast for about 15 more minutes at 150°C until golden and the thickest part reaches at least 74°C.
Rest the chicken for 5–10 minutes, cut into serving pieces and serve hot. If using a charcoal grill, turn it regularly so it cooks evenly.

canh-bi-do-nau-tom-tuoi.name: Pumpkin Soup with Fresh Shrimp
canh-bi-do-nau-tom-tuoi.serving_basis: One small pot of soup for two people as part of a family meal.
canh-bi-do-nau-tom-tuoi.description: Fresh shrimp are briefly sauteed before simmering with pumpkin, making a gently sweet broth and soft, nutty pumpkin pieces. This small serving is easy to scale up.
canh-bi-do-nau-tom-tuoi.finished_dish: The pumpkin is soft but still holds its shape, the shrimp are pink and firm, and the broth is clear with a mild natural sweetness.
canh-bi-do-nau-tom-tuoi.serving: Ladle into a bowl, sprinkle with scallions or sawtooth coriander and serve hot with rice.
tips: Cut the pumpkin into evenly sized pieces that are not too small so they do not break down during cooking.
Saute the shrimp until firm before adding water, and skim the broth to keep it clear.
Add the pumpkin after the broth boils and cook only until tender, then adjust the seasoning.
canh-bi-do-nau-tom-tuoi.image_alt: A bowl of pumpkin soup with fresh shrimp, orange pumpkin pieces and pink shrimp in clear broth.
canh-bi-do-nau-tom-tuoi.time_note: About 50 minutes; simmer the pumpkin until tender while keeping the pieces intact.

ingredients.name: Pumpkin
ingredients.notes: Peel, remove the seeds, rinse and cut into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Fresh shrimp
ingredients.notes: Remove heads, shells and vein; mince or chop if desired.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Adjust to the preferred soup consistency.

ingredients.name: Seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Reduce if using a salty stock or fish sauce.

preparation_steps: Peel and seed the pumpkin, rinse and cut it into bite-size pieces. Peel the shrimp, remove the vein, rinse and drain.
Thinly slice the shallot. Marinate the shrimp with the shallot, a little salt and seasoning powder for about 10 minutes.
cooking_steps: Heat the oil, saute the shallot until fragrant, then add the shrimp and cook until firm.
Add the water and bring to a boil, skimming foam to keep the broth clear. Add the pumpkin, cover and simmer for about 10 minutes until just tender.
Adjust with salt, seasoning powder and optional monosodium glutamate. Turn off the heat, add scallions and sawtooth coriander, and ladle into a bowl.
